verdict.rationale: PlayCanvas's plans list 'Project Archive and Restore', 'Download Apps for Self-hosting' and REST API access. The engine those apps run on is open-source and MIT-licensed, so a downloaded build can run without the service. Community evidence also points to playcanvas-sync for mirroring project assets to the local file system. However, nothing documents what the project archive contains, whether its format is open, or whether it captures all Editor data (scenes, assets, history), and these features appear only as plan bullet points; earlier community worries about code living on PlayCanvas servers are reflected in confidence, not as a dispute. missing for 10: documented contents and open format of the project archive, a confirmed complete export path for all Editor data, and independent hands-on reports of a successful migration off the platform.
